entities.summary: Cornelius Berenberg (1634–1711) was a Hamburg grand burgher, merchant banker, a member of the Berenberg family, and owner of Berenberg Bank. His grandfather Hans Berenberg (1561–1626) had fled from Antwerp with his brother Paul Berenberg (1566–1645) and established the Berenberg merchant house in Hamburg. In Hamburg, the Berenberg family formed part of the Dutch merchant colony. Cornelius Berenberg was the first to engage in merchant banking. He developed the company into a very successful merchant house and merchant bank, and forged trade links with France, Spain, Portugal, Italy, Scandinavia and Russia.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent merchant banker and member of the influential Berenberg family, Cornelius Berenberg played a significant role in shaping Hamburg's economic landscape. His establishment of Berenberg Bank forged trade links with major European powers, contributing to the growth of global commerce.
